# Sampling {.unnumbered}

```{r set}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(flextable)
library(scales)
```


```{r data}
#| message: false
# inventory
inventory <- readxl::read_excel("data/raw/inventory/inventory_Belterra_20260618.xlsx",
                                sheet = "22092026") %>% 
  select(PLACA, NOME_COMUM, NOME_CIENTIFICO, FAMILIA, 
         CAP1, CAP2, CAP3, CAP4, CAP5, CAP6, CAP7, E, N) %>% 
  mutate(across(num_range("CAP", 1:7), as.numeric)) %>% 
  rename(tree = PLACA,
         vernacular = NOME_COMUM,
         botanical = NOME_CIENTIFICO,
         family = FAMILIA,
         x_utm = E,
         y_utm = N) %>% 
  mutate(botanical = str_extract(botanical, "^\\S+\\s+\\S+"), 
         bota_code = paste0(
           str_sub(word(botanical, 1), 1, 2),
           str_sub(word(botanical, 2), 1, 2)),
         label = paste0(bota_code, "_", tree),
         botanical = replace_values(botanical, "Byrsonima crassifólia" ~ "Byrsonima crassifolia"),
         bota_code = replace_values(bota_code, "NANA" ~ NA)) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(dbh = max(CAP1, CAP2, CAP3, CAP4, CAP5, CAP6, CAP7)/pi) %>% 
  select(tree, x_utm, y_utm, 
         vernacular, botanical, family, bota_code, label, dbh) %>% 
  ungroup() # to remove row_wise

# inventory %>% group_by(bota_code) %>% summarise(n = n_distinct(botanical)) %>% filter(n>1)

# spatial object
spat_file <- "data/raw/geographic/inventory_Belterra_20260922.gpkg"
roads <- read_sf(spat_file, "EstradasdoPPesquisa")
path <- read_sf(spat_file, "TrilhaParqPesq")
inventory <- inventory %>% 
  st_as_sf(coords = c("x_utm", "y_utm"), crs = 31981)

n_tree_tot <- length(unique(inventory$tree))
```

These sampling choices are made considering the inventory data of the 22/09/2026.
This inventory contains `r n_tree_tot` individuals <!-- one duplicaed tree ID but for pinus --> .
For multistemed trees, we consider only the DBH of the bigger stem.

Unlike in 2025, the sampling is decided based on the botanical names
(as identification as occurred since). 
There are `r n_distinct(inventory$botanical, na.rm=TRUE)` different species,
with `r inventory %>% filter(is.na(botanical)) %>% nrow()` unidentified tree.
We add a botanical code using the two first letters of the genus and species.
We also add a label using the botanical code and the tree ID, that will be used for sampling.
*NB: in the field, only the tree ID is displayed on the trees.*

We also use the version 1 of cleaned data from [field campaign of 2025](20_belterra25/26_junction) and the list of planted species [TO DO everything needs to be updated once this file is checked]{style="color: red;"}.


```{r}
#| message: false
meas_2025 <- read_csv("outputs/trait_PlantForAdapt_Belterra_2025_v1.csv") %>% 
  mutate(botanical = str_extract(botanical, "^\\S+\\s+\\S+")) %>% 
  group_by(tree, botanical, verna_code) %>% 
  summarise(n_la_2025 = sum(!is.na(la)),
            n_ldmc_2025 = sum(!is.na(ldmc)),
            n_lt_2025 = sum(!is.na(lt)),
            n_sla_2025 = sum(!is.na(sla)),
            n_tlp_2025 = sum(!is.na(tlp))) %>% 
  ungroup()
inventory <- inventory %>% 
  left_join(meas_2025)

planted <- readxl::read_excel("data/raw/inventory/planted_sp_Belterra.xlsx",
                              sheet = "planted_sp_Belterra",
                              na = c("", "NA")) %>% 
  mutate(across(c(planted, ppd_sen, native) , as.logical))
  
inventory <- inventory %>% 
  left_join(planted)
```


## Objective

The functional traits will be used to:

* characterize the ecological strategies of native tree species in order to explain species demography and response to climate (T1.1)

* predict the outcome of species interactions on tree performances under drought (T2.1)

For the first objectives, we can focus in the planted species, 
but for the second, covering as much as possible the diversity of all species (planted or naturally regenerating) is important.
We will therefore aim to sample  all the planted species, and non-planted species representing the highest proportion of the stem number that we can achieve.

We will sample on minimum of 5 trees per species and per sites to account for intraspecific variability. 
However, to minimise the effect of ontogentic trait variations, we will standardise this by sampling on the biggest individuals (as a proxy for the tallest).
[TO DO: check for non-planted species that we are not sampling on too yound individuals.]{style="color: red;"}

The traits to measure are listed on this [page](11_traits), on 5 leaves per individual, except for TLP for which we take only two leaves and [Gmin]{style="color: red;"}.
For wood density, we take two wood cores per individual.

This second field campaign in Belterra aims at complementing the [field campaign of 2025](20_belterra25).


## Maps of all species

Maps of species distribution to get a visual impression of the mixture, including planted and non-planted species.

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = roads) +
  geom_sf(data = path) +
  geom_sf(data = inventory, aes(col = bota_code), size = 0.5) +
  theme_bw() + 
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```


Maps of planted species versus non planted (*NB: the information is at the species level and not available at the tree level*):

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = roads) +
  geom_sf(data = path) +
  geom_sf(data = inventory, aes(col = planted), size = 0.5) +
  theme_bw() + 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Maps of the native versus exotic species:

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = roads) +
  geom_sf(data = path) +
  geom_sf(data = inventory, aes(col = native), size = 0.5) +
  theme_bw() + 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

As the exotic species are not mixed with the native ones, we don't need to sample traits on them (even for calculating neighbourhood indices).

## Species choice

```{r}
abd <- inventory %>% 
  st_drop_geometry() %>% 
  filter(!is.na(botanical)) %>% 
  count(botanical, bota_code, planted, ppd_sen, native) %>% 
  arrange(desc(n)) %>% 
  mutate(prop = n/n_tree_tot,
         cum_prop = cumsum(prop),
         sampled_2025 = ifelse(botanical %in% unique(meas_2025$botanical),
                               TRUE,
                               FALSE))
```


### Planted

The graph below show the abundance of native species that were planted (red dashed line indicates a number of individuals currently alive of 50).
As the exotic species are not mixed with the native ones, we don't consider them (even for studying the neighbourhood) so we won't sample them.

```{r}
abd %>% 
  filter(planted == TRUE & native == TRUE) %>% 
  mutate(botanical = fct_reorder(botanical, n)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y =  botanical, 
             fill = sampled_2025, col = ppd_sen)) + 
  geom_col(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "forestgreen", `FALSE` = "grey70")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "black", `FALSE` = NA)) + 
  geom_vline(xintercept=50, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.5, col = "red") + 
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# create a table of species to sample
sampling <- abd %>% 
  filter(planted == TRUE & native == TRUE & sampled_2025 == FALSE & n>= 50) %>% 
  select(botanical, bota_code, planted, sampled_2025, n) %>% 
  mutate(n_ind_leaf = 5)
# n is the total number of living trees, n_ind_leaf is the number of individuals to sample on.
```


> Proposition 1:
Sample all the native species that were planted, that currently have at least 50 living individuals and that were not sampled in 2025.
This concerns the `r nrow(sampling)` following species : `r sampling$botanical`.

*We could consider lowering the cutoff of 50, but the 3 most abundant ones with less than 50 tress are the following:*

```{r}
abd %>% 
  filter(planted == TRUE & native == TRUE & sampled_2025 == FALSE & n < 50) %>% 
  slice_head(n = 3) %>% 
  flextable() %>% 
  autofit()
```

### Non-planted

```{r}
# nb of indiv of the species with > 0.9 of proportion cumulated
cutoff_prop <- abd %>% filter(cum_prop > 0.9) %>% slice_max(n) %>% pull(n)
```


The graph below show the abundance of species that were not planted: red dashed line indicates a number of individuals currently alive of 50 and the purple dashed line indicates a cut-off corresponding to a cumulative proportion of trees of 90%.
We assume that all the non-planted species are native [Lucas, Jessica, what do you think ? This can be checked if necessary.]{style="color: red;"}


```{r}
abd %>% 
  filter(planted == FALSE) %>% 
  mutate(botanical = fct_reorder(botanical, n)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y =  botanical, 
             fill = sampled_2025, col = ppd_sen)) + 
  geom_col(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "forestgreen", `FALSE` = "grey70")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "black", `FALSE` = NA)) + 
  geom_vline(xintercept=50, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.5, col = "red") + 
  geom_vline(xintercept=cutoff_prop, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.5, col = "purple") + 
  theme_minimal()
```


```{r}
# create a table of species to sample
sampling_no_plant <- abd %>% 
  filter(planted == FALSE & sampled_2025 == FALSE & n>= 50) %>% 
  select(botanical, bota_code, planted, sampled_2025, n) %>% 
  mutate(n_ind_leaf = 5)
sampling <- rbind(sampling, sampling_no_plant)
```

> Proposition 2:
Sample all the non-planted species that currently have at least 50 living individuals and that were not sampled in 2025.
This concerns the `r nrow(sampling_no_plant)` following species : `r sampling_no_plant$botanical`.

*We could consider lowering the cutoff of 50, the 5 most abundant ones with less than 50 tress are the following:*

```{r}
abd %>% 
  filter(planted == FALSE & sampled_2025 == FALSE & n < 50) %>% 
  slice_head(n = 5) %>% 
  flextable() %>% 
  autofit()
```


## Species with not enough individuals or leaves in 2025 campaign

### Not enough individuals

Number of individuals with a least one leaf with a valid trait measurment, per species and per trait:

```{r}
pal <- col_numeric(c("tomato", "gold", "forestgreen"), domain = c(0, 5))

meas_ind <- meas_2025 %>%          
  group_by(botanical) %>%
  summarise(across(c(n_la_2025, n_ldmc_2025, n_lt_2025, n_sla_2025, n_tlp_2025),
                   ~ sum(.x != 0)),
            .groups = "drop_last") %>% 
  left_join(select(abd, botanical, bota_code, planted, ppd_sen, sampled_2025, n), by = "botanical")

meas_ind %>% 
  select(-bota_code, -sampled_2025) %>% 
  flextable() %>% 
  bg(j = c("n_la_2025", "n_ldmc_2025", "n_lt_2025", "n_sla_2025", "n_tlp_2025"),
     bg = function(x) pal(pmin(x, 5)),
     part = "body") %>% 
  autofit()
```

*NB: Vochysia maxima has 10 individuals because it was sampled under two different vernacular names.*

> Proposition 3: keeping the same cutoff of 50 living individuals, we can sample the following species with n_ind_leaf trees to complement the sampling of 2025 :

```{r}
sampling_suppl <- meas_ind %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(n_ind_leaf = 5 - max(n_la_2025, n_ldmc_2025, n_lt_2025, n_sla_2025, n_tlp_2025)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  filter(n>= 50 & n_ind_leaf > 0 & n_la_2025 !=10) %>% 
  select(botanical, bota_code, planted, sampled_2025, n, n_ind_leaf) 
sampling <- rbind(sampling, sampling_suppl)
sampling_suppl %>% 
  flextable() %>% 
  autofit()
```

### Not enough leaves

Mean number of leaves with a valid trait measurment accross individuals with a least one leaf with a valid trait measurment, per species and per trait: 

```{r}
meas_leaf <- meas_2025 %>%          
  group_by(botanical) %>%
  summarise(across(c(n_la_2025, n_ldmc_2025, n_lt_2025, n_sla_2025, n_tlp_2025),
                   ~ round(mean(.x[.x != 0]), 2)),
            .groups = "drop_last") %>% 
  left_join(select(abd, botanical, bota_code, planted, ppd_sen, sampled_2025, n), by = "botanical")

meas_leaf %>% 
  select(-bota_code, -sampled_2025) %>% 
  flextable() %>% 
  bg(j = c("n_la_2025", "n_ldmc_2025", "n_lt_2025", "n_sla_2025"),
     bg = col_numeric(c("tomato", "gold", "forestgreen"), domain = c(0, 5)),
     part = "body") %>% 
  bg(j = "n_tlp_2025",
     bg = col_numeric(c("tomato", "gold", "forestgreen"), domain = c(0, 2)),
     part = "body") %>% 
  autofit()
```

Based on the mean number of leaves per individuals, and keeping the threshold of 50 living individuals, we could condider supplementing the number of leaves of these species:

```{r}
meas_2025 %>% 
  select(-verna_code) %>% 
  filter(botanical %in% c("Bertholletia excelsa", "Copaifera reticulata", "Jacaranda copaia")) %>% 
  arrange(botanical) %>% 
  flextable() %>% 
  bg(j = c("n_la_2025", "n_ldmc_2025", "n_lt_2025", "n_sla_2025"),
     bg = col_numeric(c("tomato", "gold", "forestgreen"), domain = c(0, 5)),
     part = "body") %>% 
  bg(j = "n_tlp_2025",
     bg = col_numeric(c("tomato", "gold", "forestgreen"), domain = c(0, 2)),
     part = "body") %>% 
  autofit()
```

> Proposition 4: Not sampling more for Bertholletia and Jacaranda, but sampling 3 new individuals of 
Copaifera.

```{r}
sampling <- sampling %>% 
  mutate(n_ind_leaf = ifelse(botanical == "Copaifera reticulata",
                             n_ind_leaf + 3,
                             n_ind_leaf))
```

## Sampling objective for leaves

The sampling counts `r sum(sampling$n_ind_leaf)` from `r nrow(sampling)` species:

```{r}
sampling %>% 
  flextable() %>% 
  autofit() 
```
